root_motivation: Joe's mcphost gate takes 21–42 minutes for a 413 s cold compile. The repo's `tests/` directory holds 289 top-level `.rs` files (2026-09-12 count) and cargo's default `autotests` makes each one a separate test binary; each links the whole 52K-LoC crate and its 41 dependencies, and measured binaries are 274–291 MB (`attrib_ac1_loopback_signup_unstamped`, `infer_ac08_ac09_python_requirements`). `target/debug/deps` holds 1,391 such binaries. 269 of the files declare `mod common;`, so the shared helper is compiled 269 times. RedBaron's root disk reached 81–86 % on 09-08, with `target/` dirs the known bulk. Every gate pays the link cost 289 times for one crate; every new AC PRD adds another binary. PRD-build-gate-phase-timing measures the `gate` phase this PRD moves; until it ships, the expected saving is inferred from binary count and size, not measured.
user_persona: An integrator (agent or human operator) who wants an external system -- GitHub, Stripe, a monitoring tool -- to reach an mcphost tool without standing up and hand-verifying a separate endpoint; secondarily the sender making the actual signed HTTP POST to the hook URL, and the operator reading /healthz's events_received_1h/events_rejected_1h after a redeploy.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the repo at HEAD, When `gen-test-suites.sh` runs and `cargo nextest list` runs, Then at most ten test binaries are listed and the set of test names (suite prefix stripped) equals the set listed at the parent commit.

Given a new file `tests/zzz_ac1_probe.rs` that is not in any suite, When `gen-test-suites.sh --check` runs, Then it exits non-zero naming `tests/zzz_ac1_probe.rs`; after regenerating, it exits 0 and the test is listed.
Given the consolidated layout, When `grep -c 'mod common' tests/*.rs` runs over the included files, Then the count is 0 and each suite file declares `mod common;` once.

Given the archived mcphost PRDs' test pointers (for example `tests/hooks_ac1_*.rs`), When the verified-completed pairing classifier runs against them, Then every pairing that resolved before resolves now.
Given a clean `target/`, When `cargo nextest run` completes, Then `du -s target/debug/deps` is under 5 GB and the receipt records the size.

Given two timed full nextest runs at the same commit, one before and one after the change (or the `gate:` phase from PRD-build-gate-phase-timing when present), When compared in the receipt, Then the after time is ≤50 % of before.
Given `.config/nextest.toml` with JUnit enabled, When the suite runs, Then a JUnit file exists with a duration per test.
Given the parity script from mcphost-tests-host-independence, When run against the new layout on one host, Then it matches by test name and reports the same test count as before.
Given the `suite` selftest cases, When the repo's test selftest runs, Then they are named and green.

scope: POST /hooks/{namespace}/{tool}: resolve the tenant by namespace and the tool by name, require an enabled event trigger on that tool, enforce MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES, verify the signature per the trigger's verify config, store the event as a run (trigger='event', status='queued'), enqueue it through the executor with args {event: {...}}, and answer 202 {run_id}; failures answer 401 signature_invalid, 404 hook_not_found, 413, or 429 events_rate_limited and never run the tool (Requirement 1).

Verification schemes hmac-sha256 (optional Stripe-style t=,v1= timestamp tolerance), hmac-sha1, token, and none (requires allow_unverified: true, labeled unverified in host.trigger.list); secrets are read through src/secrets.rs and never logged (Requirement 2).

The host.trigger.* tool surface: set(kind="event", tool, verify, args?) returns the hook URL; list/get/pause/resume/remove shared with schedules; test(id, body, headers) and replay(run_id) (Requirement 3).
Plan-derived ceilings -- event_triggers_max, events_per_minute (per trigger), event_body_bytes_max -- with named refusals, surfaced in host.quickstart's limits (Requirement 4).

Header-allowlist redaction on stored events and the tenant's existing state-quota rules (Requirement 5); /healthz gains events_received_1h/events_rejected_1h and host.usage counts event runs (Requirement 6).
P1: dedupe_header idempotency -- a repeated delivery id within 24h answers 202 with the original run id and does not run again (Requirement 7).
non_goals: Outbound webhooks (a tool posting to others); the http kind does that already.
Email, queue or socket ingress; the trigger model leaves room.
Custom verification code in the first version; unsupported schemes use `none` with an explicit opt-in.

The Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Instant>>> state EventCounters/EventRateLimiter added in commit 3b07bdd ('mcphost: v0.44.0 -- a tool has a public URL that checks the signature and runs the tool with the event') is accepted without further commit-message rationale: it is justified in-code via doc comments citing the pre-existing ToolRunLimiter precedent, and reviewer-agent's falsification.panic_audit/public_api_audit found no correctness issue from it. reviewer-agent concern id `arc-mutex-added-without-commit-message-justification` (receipt captured_at 2026-09-12T04:59:52Z) is the rule-4 signal this records as accepted, per PRD-mcphost-reviewer-debt-paydown Requirement 2 / AC3.

additional.no_panic_in_src: BAD_RUST denies unwrap/expect/panic in src/; the hooks.rs header-forwarding path handles HeaderValue::from_str fallibly (hooks.rs:806, `let (Ok(name), Ok(val)) = (...) else { continue }`), not via unwrap -- confirmed by reviewer-agent's panic_audit at HEAD d1b35ae.
additional.secrets_never_logged: AC2: a signature-verification failure must never log the secret; src/secrets.rs is the sole read path and hooks.rs contains zero tracing::*! call sites in the verification path.
additional.constant_time_signature_compare: Signature comparison uses constant_time_eq rather than a short-circuiting `==`, and the length check ahead of it leaks only the fixed-width hex digest length, not the secret's length (reviewer-agent public_api_audit).
additional.one_event_trigger_per_tool: host.trigger.set enforces the plan's event_triggers_max and a single-event-trigger-per-tool invariant before insertion; reviewer-agent's falsification.counter_attack notes this check-then-insert is not yet guarded against a concurrent-call race, logged as an open concern, not a MUST-level block.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't an integrator connect GitHub, Stripe or a monitoring system to a tool on mcphost?
five_whys_trace.a: A tool call only ever enters through /mcp with a key; nothing outside mcphost can wake a tool, so the integrator has no URL to point an external sender at.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no such URL?
five_whys_trace.a: The router (src/http.rs) serves only /mcp, /healthz, /.well-known/mcp/{namespace}/server.json, and the billing webhook and pages -- there is no tenant-facing inbound route for a tool.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did integrators have to solve this themselves before now?
five_whys_trace.a: Without a built-in route, they would have to stand up an endpoint elsewhere and hand-verify HMAC or token signatures -- exactly the work the capability panel's integrator segment said they came to mcphost to stop doing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why prioritize this gap now rather than later?
five_whys_trace.a: The integrator segment topped switch-share in both the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-09 discover packs, and its stated gate was explicit: 'webhook signature verification built in... I paste the secret, you handle it.'

five_whys_trace.q: Why hadn't a webhook route shipped already, given the demand?
five_whys_trace.a: It depended on groundwork that had only just landed: the triggers table and host.trigger.* tool surface were introduced by PRD-mcphost-schedules (the first trigger kind), and PRD-mcphost-runs-and-jobs' run model; this PRD is the second kind of trigger built on that surface (Depends-on both).

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
